newsitem.title: USA: Revco signs pact for access to Big B data.
newsitem.headline: Revco signs pact for access to Big B data.

text.p: Revco D.S. Inc., which has launched a $332 million hostile takeover of Big B Inc., said Friday it has signed an agreement that will give it access to some of the regional drugstore chain's confidential financial data.

Big B, which last month rejected Revco's offer as financially inadequate, has signed similar pacts with other potential bidders and indicated that those parties are willing to pay more than the $15 per share offered by Revco.
Revco and Big B had been haggling over the terms of a confidentiality agreement for several weeks.

"We expect that the confidentiality agreement with Big B will allow us to work on a level playing field toward our goal of negotiating a transaction that is enthusiastically supported by Big B's shareholders and employees, as well as Big B's many loyal customers," Revco chief executive officer Dwayne Hoven said in a news release.
Twinsburg, Ohio-based Revco is the nation's second-largest drugstore chain. Big B, based in Bessemer, Ala., operates in the Southeast.
As part of the agreement, Revco said it will not start a proxy solicitiation or take any other actions to gain control of Big B, other than the tender offer, until Nov. 30.
The confidentiality agreement also calls a temporary halt to federal litigation filed by both companies over Big B's poison pill antitakeover plan.

Revco also said it has extended its tender offer for Big B, which had been set to expire on Oct. 7, until Oct. 18. Revco said that as of Oct. 3, 53,300 shares of Big B stock had been tendered to Revco under its offer.

Big B's stock was unchanged at $16.75 on Nasdaq in late morning trading. The stock has risen in the past month on speculation that Big B will be sold at a price above the $15 per share offered by Revco.
Revco edged up 25 cents $29.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
